units.name: FillAttributes
units.summary: A selects nametable high byte; add 3 and use low byte $C0. Fill the 64-byte attribute table with X.

units.name: CopyAttributes
units.summary: Copy 64 attribute bytes from sourcePtr to the selected nametable's $3C0 offset.

units.name: ReadAttributes
units.summary: Read 64 attributes into attributeShadow after discarding the PPU read-buffer byte. Save the destination address for later NMI updates.

units.name: SeedRandom
units.summary: Initialize the two-byte random state to $110E.

units.name: NextRandom
units.summary: Advance an eight-step shift/XOR generator using feedback $B4. Preserve Y; return the new high state byte in A.

units.name: DecodeNametableRuns
units.summary: Decode a compact stream directly to PPUDATA. The first five bytes are dictionary values; zero ends the stream. Commands use low five bits as count: $E0 repeats the next byte, $C0 increments from it, $A0 copies literals, other high groups repeat a dictionary byte. Source pointers advance between commands.

units.name: DecodeRunCommand
units.summary: Choose repeat, incrementing, literal or dictionary mode from the command's high three bits.

units.name: LoadPalettes
units.summary: Copy 16 bytes from each of sourcePtr and secondaryPtr into adjacent background/sprite palette shadows, then upload all 32 colors.

units.name: UploadPalettes
units.summary: Wait for vblank, write all 32 shadow colors to $3F00, then perform the palette-address reset sequence.

units.name: EnqueueVramTransfer
units.summary: Copy the eight-byte descriptor at queueDescriptorPtr into a 32-slot ring. Carry set means full; carry clear means accepted. One slot remains unused to distinguish full from empty.

units.name: CopyQueueDescriptor
units.summary: Select producer index times eight and copy the descriptor; advance producer modulo 32.

units.name: DrainVramTransfers
units.summary: NMI consumes all pending eight-byte descriptors. Fields are PPU address low/high, byte count, reserved byte, RAM pointer low/high, stride mode, direction. Direction zero writes RAM to PPU; nonzero reads PPU into RAM with a dummy buffered read. Restore software stride after draining.

units.name: ConsumeQueueDescriptor
units.summary: Load count and RAM pointer, select PPU increment 1 or 32 without enabling NMI, then execute the requested transfer.

units.name: WriteQueuedBytes
units.summary: Write count bytes from transferPtr to PPUDATA; count zero wraps to 256 bytes.

units.name: ReadQueuedBytes
units.summary: Discard the first buffered PPU read, then copy count bytes into transferPtr.

units.name: AdvanceQueueConsumer
units.summary: Reset PPU address to $2000 and advance consumer modulo 32 before checking for another descriptor.

units.name: UploadDirtyAttributes
units.summary: Clear the dirty flag and write all 64 attribute shadow bytes, eight at a time, using increment 1. NMI later restores PPUCTRL and scroll.

units.name: TickAudio
units.summary: Run music and effect sequencing once per NMI.

units.name: TickMusic
units.summary: If active, decrement the event delay. A due event decodes packed channel/note records; otherwise reduce active note lengths and silence expired voices.

units.name: TickNoteLength
units.summary: Y selects a music channel. Leave it alone while an effect owns that channel; otherwise count down its length, silence on expiry and clear its active-mask bit.

units.name: DecodeMusicEvents
units.summary: Read note/channel, duration and next-delay triples. Zero duration ends a pattern and advances or loops the song. Zero next-delay batches simultaneous notes; pending-mask bits determine which hardware voices to update.

units.name: StageMusicNote
units.summary: The high two note bits select channel, low six bits plus transposition select pitch. Save doubled pitch index and duration, and mark the channel active and pending.

units.name: WritePendingMusicNotes
units.summary: Send only newly staged voices to hardware, skipping any channel currently reserved by a sound effect.

units.name: WriteMusicPitch
units.summary: A selects voice and Y indexes pitch words. Pulse and triangle use timer tables; noise uses the fixed noise setup. An active effect takes priority over music on its voice.

units.name: StartSoundEffect
units.summary: A selects an effect pointer. Request termination of an existing effect and wait a frame before replacement. Header selects voice and initial register bytes; subsequent stream records are timed pitches or control changes.

units.name: TickSoundEffect
units.summary: Count down effect delay; $FF or a negative activity flag terminates and restores music instrument state. $FE changes control bytes; other values select a pitch with a following duration byte.

units.name: FinishSoundEffect
units.summary: Silence the effect voice, restore the saved music instrument control bytes and clear effect activity.

units.name: DecodeEffectRecord
units.summary: Interpret $FE as a three-byte control command; otherwise write a pitch-table pair and take the next byte as delay.
